findings.title: Graph-v9 verification remains bound to the graph-v8 controller state namespace
findings.criterion_ref: Criterion 1 — “v9 must use distinct graph/contract/schema/prompt/result/state lineage without overwriting v8 evidence”; also defeats Criterion 11 entry safety for the real N70/N80 path.
findings.trigger: Run the advertised fresh cascade with `.run27_state_v9`, then execute any graph-declared N70/N80/N90 controller verification command. Those commands omit `--state-dir`, so the controller defaults to the existing `.run27_state` containing graph-v8 receipts. Alternatively, running the whole cascade with controller defaults mixes v9 admissions into that v8 state namespace.
findings.consequence: A genuinely separate v9 cascade cannot pass its declared N70/N80/N90 verification because those checks inspect v8 ancestor receipts and report changed lineage. Using the default throughout instead replaces current receipt files and mixes v9 attempts/audit events into v8 state, so the required distinct state lineage is not preserved.
findings.evidence: The bundle claims `.run27_state_v9/` at rc12_review_bundle.v1.md line 62, but controller/core.py line 29 defines `DEFAULT_STATE_DIR` as `.run27_state`, and run27_controller.py line 236 uses that default. Graph-v9 commands at implementation.graph.v9.yaml lines 301, 313, and 326 pass `--graph` but no `--state-dir`. A direct read-only invocation of graph-v9 `status` loaded the existing N00 receipt from `results/v8/`, whose `graph_sha256` is the required v8 digest `c2d79a…`, and reported `lineage_fingerprint_changed` rather than a fresh no-receipt v9 state.

observations: All advertised live digests recomputed exactly, including the immutable graph-v8 digest and graph-v9/schema-v6/contract-v6/specification digests.
The real plan validator passed; the complete-tree security scan reported zero violations; and the integration-ownership validator passed all 75 claims.

The exact cited focused suite passed 792 tests and the package suite passed 175 tests. The initial nested-sandbox limitation disappeared when the exact focused suite was rerun outside the outer QA sandbox, so it was not raised as a finding.
reasoning: Execution corroborated the domain verifier, repair/retest, physical-store, replay, package-binding, ownership, and regression claims. The surviving blocker is outside those green suites: the advertised v9 state namespace is not bound into either the controller default or the graph’s live-proof/final-audit commands. Thus no invocation strategy simultaneously provides distinct v9 state and executes the declared real N70/N80/N90 verification against that state.
